title: A failed step on the strip is drawn as a cross too small to see
foundBy: user report (maintainer): "It's a very ugly x and isn't easy to spot", with a design another agent built on a consuming page

evidence.verified:
The attended corpus was exported with the new build and the page for its longest session opened headlessly at a failed tool call, in dark and in light. In the ordinary view the failed step is a bar in the error colour at its own height, with nothing inside or above it, ringed by the selection. With errors only on it stands at the top of its row with a dot above it, and every other bar is dimmed. The ring wraps the whole tall bar and the dot. The dot sits inside the canvas in both themes, since the row keeps six pixels above the tallest bar. The errors control beside the kind chips and the index legend both show a plain square in the error colour, and the failed card's title mark is the same square.

Unit tests pin the mapping. A failed step becomes its own kind painted in the error colour with no cross. It rises to the ceiling with a dot only when errors only is on, and the ceiling leaves headroom. A spawn's marker takes another colour, and a kind chip hides its failed steps too. The card mark test asserts the error fill with nothing drawn inside. `make ci` passes: parity PASS on three runs, and every fixture check passes, 27 ok and 9 met. One budget moved: the ui build the mark needs is 16 KB larger, and the maintainer raised the large-session page budget to 1,500,000 bytes.

resolution: A failed step is drawn in the error colour, never as a glyph inside the cell (R47). With errors only on it rises to the top of its row with a dot of that colour above it, and everything else dims. When selected, the taller bar is ringed whole. The legend key and the card's title mark are the same plain square. The treatment matches the other consumer of the strip component, which the maintainer reviewed against this one. The dot's colour comes from the marker token in the ui build this record moved tracer's pin to.
details:
A failed step is marked by a cross painted inside its cell over the kind colour (R47). At the strip's cell width of 13 pixels the cross is two thin strokes inside a bar a few pixels wide. A reader scanning for failures does not find them. A mock of the same synthetic run showed three failures among forty events; with the cross they were all but invisible at real size.

The agreed design, from another agent's page and a mock the maintainer reviewed:

- In the ordinary view a failed step takes the error colour as its fill, at its real height, and nothing is drawn inside or above it. Colour is what the eye finds.
- With errors only on, a failed step is drawn at full lane height with a dot of the error colour above it, and everything else is dimmed, so failures stand out at any zoom. Height means time in the ordinary view and means failure in this mode, which is explicit.
- The dot must never be clipped, at the top of a lane, at either end of the strip, or when the strip scrolls.
- When a failed step is selected in errors-only mode, the selection highlight must cover the full-height bar, not the bar's ordinary height.

R47 is rewritten, since it forbids replacing the kind fill. The legend's cross entry becomes a plain error swatch. The card's own mark, which mirrors its cell so the two can be matched, takes the same treatment. The dot's colour comes from the marker token the ui component gained on 2026-09-22, which is not yet in a published build. So ui publishes first, then tracer's pin moves, then the strip changes. The pixel parity gate and the fixture checks that read the strip will move and need approval.

notes.text: In the mock the maintainer reviewed, the dot was in the accent colour. The other consumer of the component draws it in the error colour, and the maintainer chose to match it, so a reader moving between the two learns one mark. A spawn's marker takes the foreground colour instead, so the two dots never read alike.

Seen on a real trace, the dot in the ordinary view looked odd. The maintainer kept it for errors only, where the raised bar is, and asked for the plain square in the errors control. That matches the other consumer, which also draws the dot only in that mode.
